title: Losses from Scams and Malware Fraud: Doing Right by Bank Customers
what_it_is: Losses from Scams and Malware Fraud: Doing Right by Bank Customers

sections.label: Scam and cyber crime statistics
sections.summary: Police 2022 annual statistics show reported scam and cyber crime cases rose 25% year on year to nearly 33,700 cases, or 92 reports daily.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Police's annual statistics for 2022, reported cases of scam and cyber crime increased by 25% year on year, totalling nearly 33,700 cases or 92 reports per day.

sections.label: MAS loss-sharing consultation plan
sections.summary: A May Parliamentary answer said MAS intended to issue a public consultation on equitable loss-sharing in the third quarter of this year.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: On the specific question of who should bear the loss of scams, we understand from a Parliamentary answer in May that the MAS intended to issue a public consultation on a framework for the equitable sharing of losses in the third quarter of this year.

sections.label: FIDReC dispute resolution timeframe
sections.summary: FIDReC, which oversees many such disputes, resolves most cases within six months.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: According to the Financial Industry Disputes Resolution Centre (FIDReC), which oversees many such disputes, most cases are resolved within six months.

sections.label: UK mandatory scam reimbursement
sections.summary: From next year UK banks must fully reimburse scam victims under a mandatory Faster Payment reimbursement model with defined conditions and timelines.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: From next year, banks in the UK will be required by law to fully reimburse scam victims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The mandatory reimbursement would cover payments through their Faster Payment platform in situations we are familiar with such as customers being tricked into transferring money, customers clicking on fake advertisements on social media, customers who were phished or hacked despite precautions and customers who were groomed over time such as love scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It will generally not require a time-consuming and resource-intensive adjudication process for each case.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: It would be limited only to certain types of domestic payments, with both the sending and receiving payment providers each sharing half of the reimbursement.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: These providers would have to do so within five business days.

sections.label: Gross negligence reimbursement exclusion
sections.summary: The reimbursement model retains individual responsibility, with no reimbursement where a customer is grossly negligent.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The reimbursement model still retains an element of individual responsibility as there will be no reimbursement where a customer is grossly negligent.

sections.label: MAS regulatory guidelines urged
sections.summary: The speaker urges MAS to adopt regulatory guidelines on fairness in scam disputes, citing NDAs, prescribed clauses and FIDReC's $100,000 claim limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: However, as a voluntary code, it lacks regulatory bite.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I urge the MAS to consider adopting regulatory guidelines to enshrine fairness as a key principle in the settlement of consumer disputes, especially in relation to scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Some possible guidelines include banning the use of onerous practices such as blanket NDAs, which require customers to give up legitimate claims to recover monies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Perhaps the MAS could consider prescribing clauses in agreements that do not prejudice customers.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: There is currently a monetary limit of $100,000 per claim for FIDReC adjudication.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Since the daily transfer limit for most customers for PayNow is $200,000 per day, would this limit not be more relevant to FIDReC today?

sections.label: FIDReC for larger claims
sections.summary: This would make FIDReC a more serious option for larger claims.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: — would make FIDReC a more serious option for larger claims.

sections.label: Government scam reimbursement measures
sections.summary: The Government should consider other jurisdictions, bank reimbursement costs, physical tokens, ring-fencing, unfair settlements and raising FIDReC's monetary limit.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: The Government should consider developments in other jurisdictions such as the UK to ensure that banks bear the cost of reimbursing victims, as they are the best place to identify and prevent such scams.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Other measures such as a return to physical tokens and ring-fencing funds from high-risk activities like cryptocurrencies should also be considered.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Lastly, the Government should provide a framework to protect customers from unfair settlements and look at raising the monetary limit of FIDReC.

sections.label: Scam losses decreased slightly
sections.summary: Total scam losses decreased slightly in the first half of 2023 compared to the same period in 2022.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The total amount of scam losses decreased slightly in the first half of 2023, compared to the same period in 2022.

sections.label: Bank anti-scam measures
sections.summary: OCBC blocks mobile banking on devices with potentially malicious apps, and banks are exploring MoneyLock.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: A recent example is OCBC’s move to block mobile banking access on devices that are detected to carry potentially malicious apps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Banks are also exploring MoneyLock, to allow customers to set aside an amount in their bank accounts which cannot be digitally transferred out without strict authentication measures.

sections.label: MAS digital system requirements
sections.summary: MAS requires banks to secure digital systems with multi-factor authentication and notification alerts to customers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: MAS requires banks to secure digital systems, including by implementing multi-factor authentication to verify a customer’s identity and to authorise online transactions; and also sending notification alerts to customers so they can report unauthorised transactions as soon as possible.

sections.label: Diligent customers avoid losses
sections.summary: Customers who practised good cyber hygiene and protected login information and OTPs should not bear losses.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: Customers who practised good cyber hygiene and were diligent in preventing their login information and OTPs from being divulged to third parties, should not have to bear losses.

sections.label: Consultation paper on phishing scams
sections.summary: The Government aims to publish a consultation paper on the framework next month, starting with phishing scams.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: While this has taken longer than we would like, the Government aims to publish a consultation paper on the framework next month, focusing on phishing scams as a start.

sections.label: Anti-scam measures and sitting time
sections.summary: The Government will implement upstream and downstream anti-scam measures with industry, possibly sacrificing convenience, and the Sitting tomorrow starts at 1.30 pm.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: The Government will spare no effort to implement effective upstream and downstream anti-scam measures alongside industry.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Culture, Community and Youth and Trade and Industry (Mr Alvin Tan)
sentences.text: In doing so, as the Member suggested, we may inevitably sacrifice some convenience to achieve better security.

sentences.speaker: Mr Speaker
sentences.text: Pursuant to Standing Order 2(3)(a), I wish to inform hon Members that the Sitting tomorrow will commence at 1.30 pm.
